title: What Happens When Your Eyelid Won't Stop Twitching?
description:
Send this to the friend whose eye has been twitching all week.
That flutter is eyelid myokymia: the eyelid muscle firing on its own (AAO EyeWiki: up to 3-8 times a second), most often in the lower lid, from a nervous-system glitch. Cleveland Clinic says it's extremely common, usually harmless, and most cases go away within days or weeks. Common triggers: poor sleep, caffeine, stress, eye strain and long screen time. See an eye doctor if it hasn't gone after a few weeks, spreads to other parts of your face, or affects your vision (right away for any vision change).
